# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 51 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 51 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_051_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 2 — The Elm and the Vine

**51:1** As I was walking in the field and observing an elm tree and a grapevine, and reflecting upon them and their fruits, the Shepherd appeared to me and said: "What are you thinking about?" "Lord," I said, "I am thinking about the elm tree and the vine, because they are so beautiful to look at."

**51:2** "These two trees," he said, "are appointed as a type for the servants of God." "Lord," I said, "I wish to know the type of the elm tree and of the grapevine, and what their types refer to." "Do you see," he said, "the elm tree and the grapevine?" "I see them, lord," I said.

**51:3** "This grapevine," he said, "bears fruit, but the elm tree is barren. Yet this vine, unless it climbs up upon the elm, cannot bear much fruit when it lies along the ground, and what it does bear is rotten, because it is not hanging upon the elm. Therefore when the vine is fastened upon the elm, it bears fruit both from itself and from the elm.

**51:4** "You see therefore that the elm also gives much fruit, no less than the vine — indeed even more." "How more, lord?" I said. "Because," he said, "the vine, hanging upon the elm, gives much fruit both good and beautiful; but when it lies upon the ground it gives little fruit, and that rotten. This similitude therefore applies to God's servants, to the poor and to the rich."

**51:5** "How so, lord? Tell me." "Listen," he said. "The rich man has wealth but is poor toward the Lord, being distracted by his riches. His prayer and his confession before the Lord are very small and weak and have no power above. But when the rich man gives to the poor man and assists him in his needs, believing that what he does to the poor man will find recompense with God — for the poor man is rich in intercession and in confession, and his intercession has great power before God — the rich man then provides all things to the poor man without wavering.

**51:6** The poor man therefore, being supplied by the rich, prays to God and gives him thanks for the one who gave to him, and that rich man goes on helping the poor man diligently, so that the poor man is not lacking in his life. For the poor man knows that the rich man is not able to pray, and gives thanks to God on behalf of the rich man for what was given to him. And the rich man, when he hears the poor man praying for him, rejoices greatly, because he knows that the poor man prays on his behalf before God."

**51:7** Both therefore perform their work — the poor man in the prayer and in the confession and in the thanksgiving, and the rich man in giving money to the poor. Both then accomplish much before the Lord. So therefore let neither the rich man hold back from giving — for as he gives, the poor man intercedes for him and the rich man is enriched by God — nor let the poor man think lightly of the prayer of the rich, for both are good when they do their work.

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the economic theology of the elm-and-vine parable.*
